key_provisions.TITLE_II: Offers and Sales of Digital Commodities — §201 Investment contract assets, §202-204 Exemptions, §205 Mature blockchain system
key_provisions.TITLE_III: SEC Registration for Intermediaries — §301-315 (treatment of stablecoins, anti-fraud, ATS eligibility, dual-registration)
key_provisions.TITLE_IV: CFTC Registration for Digital Commodity Intermediaries — §401-415 (qualified digital asset custodians, futures commission merchants, digital commodity exchanges, brokers, dealers, associated persons, commodity pool operators)
key_provisions.TITLE_V: Innovation and Technology Improvements — §501-512 (Strategic Hub for Innovation and Financial Technology, LabCFTC codification, DeFi study, NFT study)
key_provisions.TITLE_VI: Anti-CBDC Surveillance State Act — §601-605 (prohibition on Fed issuing CBDC directly or indirectly)

sources_researched.ethics_additions: Tillis-Gallego ethics proposal language + Treasury authority to prevent deposit flight + BRCA (Blockchain Regulatory Certainty Act) civil safe harbor + affiliate trading guardrails
sources_researched.jurisdiction_split: SEC (Titles I, III) + CFTC (Titles I, IV) + Treasury (Title VI)

key_provisions.payment_stablecoin_definition: digital asset (i) used as means of payment or settlement, (ii) issued by permitted payment stablecoin issuer
key_provisions.reserve_requirement: 1:1 USD — coins, currency, deposits at insured banks, short-dated T-bills, repos, reverse repos, MMFs, central bank reserves
key_provisions.custody_segregation: Required — no commingling with own funds (with exceptions)
key_provisions.bankruptcy_priority: Stablecoin holders have priority over ALL other claims against issuer
key_provisions.foreign_issuer: Section 18(a) — foreign issuer may offer if Treasury determines comparable regime + OCC registration
key_provisions.DASPs: Digital Asset Service Providers — only offer foreign stablecoins with comparable reciprocal arrangement
key_provisions.AML: FinCEN must facilitate novel methods to detect illicit activity
key_provisions.implementation: Treasury 12 CFR Chapter XV Part 1523 — proposed Aug 2026

sources_researched.framework: SEC Regulation Crypto Assets (Release 33-11434, File S7-2026-27)

key_provisions.Subpart_B_startup_exemption: Up to $5M raised over rolling 4 years, no financial statements required, no non-accredited investor cap
key_provisions.Subpart_C_tier_1_fundraising: Up to $20M / 12 months, $6M affiliate cap, financial statements required, 10% income/net worth non-accredited cap, U.S.-anchored required
key_provisions.Subpart_C_tier_2_fundraising: Up to $75M / 12 months, $22.5M affiliate cap, financial statements required, 10% income/net worth non-accredited cap, U.S.-anchored required
key_provisions.Proposed_Rule_400: Conditional safe harbor from 'investment contract' definition — issuer can certify essential managerial efforts completed/ceased
key_provisions.First_year_selling_securityholder: Limited to 30% of aggregate offering price
key_provisions.Disclosure_Rule_103: Principles-based narrative: terms, crypto asset mechanics + source code, token economics + supply + governance, management + conflicts, risk factors with annual updates within 30 days
key_provisions.State_preemption: Preempts state securities law registration/qualification if within exemptions

sources_researched.U.S._anchored_requirements: U.S. citizens/residents >50% assets in U.S., business principally administered domestically
sources_researched.SEC_commissioners: Atkins, Peirce, Uyeda (all-Republican panel after Crenshaw departed Jan 2, 2026)

key_technical_details.iso_20022: Integration with Swift's ISO 20022 messaging infrastructure (already deployed via Chainlink pilot with UBS Tokenize)
